title: EIP-8253: Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts
description: Set nonce to 1 for accounts with empty code, zero nonce, and non-empty storage via an irregular state transition
author: Jochem Brouwer (@jochem-brouwer)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract At the start of the designated fork block, set the nonce to `1` for a per-chain, configured list of accounts that have empty code, zero nonce, and non-empty storage. Bumping the nonce restores the invariant that zero nonce and empty code imply empty storage: the accounts then fail the [EIP-684](./eip-684.md) precondition for contract creation (`nonce == 0`), so no runtime storage check at contract creation is needed. ## Motivation [EIP-684](./eip-684.md) requires zero nonce and zero code length at a `CREATE` destination. Pre-[EIP-161](./eip-161.md), `CREATE` did not increment the nonce before init code ran, so a constructor that wrote storage and returned no code left an account with zero nonce and non-empty storage. This is the only shape where zero nonce and empty code do not imply empty storage; a creation landing on it would inherit that storage. The alternative fix is to additionally require empty storage at the destination of every contract creation. This however needs an extra check in runtime code, and for some clients/database layouts also another disk read, which is paid forever, guarding against a non-growing address set after Spurious Dragon. This EIP restores the invariant with a one-time, per-account nonce bump. After the fork, the targeted accounts have `nonce == 1`, so EIP-684 rejects any future `CREATE`/`CREATE2` to them and no runtime storage check is required. The targeted addresses are unreachable on Mainnet (see Security Considerations); the purpose is to retire the shape. The motivation parallels [EIP-7523](./eip-7523.md), which similarly cleaned up empty accounts to retire EIP-161's "touch" edge cases from re-execution and test logic. Removing this account shape from future state likewise retires the analysis and test-case burden it imposes on subsequent EIPs. ## Specification The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119). ### Account list The list of targeted accounts is a chain configuration parameter, in the same way as system contract addresses. For a given chain, the list MUST contain exactly the accounts that satisfy all of the following in the pre-state of the fork block: - `nonce == 0`, - `codeHash == keccak256("")` (`EmptyCodeHash`), - `storageRoot != keccak256(RLP(""))` (`EmptyRootHash`). Such accounts can only be produced by a contract creation before [EIP-161](./eip-161.md), or by a genesis allocation. A chain on which EIP-161 has been active since genesis, and whose genesis does not allocate accounts of this shape, has an empty list; on such a chain this EIP is a no-op. The list of one chain MUST NOT be reused on another chain without re-deriving it against that chain's state (see Security Considerations). ### Mainnet account list The targeted Mainnet accounts are published as [`targeted-accounts.json`](../assets/eip-8253/targeted-accounts.json) (28 entries). Each entry contains the 20-byte address and its `keccak256` hash. The published file additionally records each account's non-zero storage slots (slot key, its hash, and its value), as supporting information for the predicate `storageRoot != EmptyRootHash`: the storage root of each account can be reconstructed from the file alone and compared to the reported root. The slot information is not used by the state transition. The construction procedure and verification (against `eth_getProof` on `latest`) are documented in [`methodology.md`](../assets/eip-8253/methodology.md). The 224-entry pre-EIP-161-deletion superset at the Spurious Dragon block is published alongside, as [`zero-nonce-matches.jsonl`](../assets/eip-8253/zero-nonce-matches.jsonl). ### State transition At the start of the fork block, before any pre-execution system contract calls (e.g. those introduced by [EIP-2935](./eip-2935.md), [EIP-4788](./eip-4788.md), [EIP-7002](./eip-7002.md), [EIP-7251](./eip-7251.md)) and before any transactions, for each account `A` in the list: 1. The nonce of `A` MUST be set to `1`. 2. `balance`, `codeHash`, and `storageRoot` of `A` are not modified. The transition is unconditional: it does not inspect `A` before writing the nonce. The list requirement above guarantees that the nonce of `A` is `0` before the transition, so the write is an increment from `0` to `1`. If the list is empty, the transition does nothing. The transition produces no transaction, receipt, or log, and consumes no gas. ### Application to non-Mainnet chains Chains that carry Mainnet state from after Spurious Dragon (including Mainnet shadow forks) apply the Mainnet list. Chains on which EIP-161 has been active since genesis, which includes all current public test networks, have an empty list. Other chains have to generate the list for their own state using the procedure in [`methodology.md`](../assets/eip-8253/methodology.md), listing both the address preimages and their hashes. Test chains and test fixtures that exercise the transition allocate accounts of the targeted shape in genesis and name them in the chain configuration, in the same way system contracts are exercised. To exercise the Mainnet list itself, [`mainnet-prestate-alloc.json`](../assets/eip-8253/mainnet-prestate-alloc.json) provides the 28 Mainnet accounts (balance, zero nonce, storage) as a genesis `alloc` fragment; a devnet that allocates these in genesis and configures the Mainnet list activates the EIP against the exact Mainnet shape of the targeted accounts. ### Interaction with [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) If [EIP-7928](./eip-7928.md) is active at the fork block, the BAL MUST encode the changes at `block_access_index = 0`, the index shared with the pre-execution system contract calls. For each targeted account `A`, the transition contributes to the `AccountChanges` entry of `A`: - `nonce_changes`: a single `NonceChange` `[0, 1]` (`block_access_index = 0`, `new_nonce = 1`); - nothing to `storage_changes`, `storage_reads`, `balance_changes`, or `code_changes`.
